content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text rules on a single-verse link (D4 vs C2 on Luke 2:48-49) as UNDERDETERMINED, which is exactly the kind of STANDS/UNDERDETERMINED ruling K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"“A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand”: I weighed whether Luke 2:48-49’s “thy father”/“my Father’s business” is one verse carrying two senses at once (not open; both stand) or merely a single verse that leaves the link unstated (not a permitted ground for UNDERDETERMINED).","why":"The judge labels the link UNDERDETERMINED by pointing to Luke 2:48-49’s two phrases as if they leave the matter open, contrary to K-S2’s command that a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand."}
